verdicts.reason: A breaks the reading order badly. The Yearly card sits above the logo, the subhead sits above the headline, and the three price cards are split up: one at the very top, one between the headline and the CTA, and one under the CTA. The cards are so small that their labels and prices are unreadable, so the pricing comparison is lost. B keeps the logo and headline at the top and puts Yearly and Family next to each other, but Monthly is left alone below the subhead. The cards are still too small to read, the price values are not legible, the subhead falls between the cards, and large dead gaps remain, so it is broken but a little more coherent than A.
